evaluationParameters: Mean arterial pressure and peripheral perfusion response
missingInformation: Whether an adequate IV fluid bolus has already been administered and the client's response
Client weight and comorbidities affecting fluid resuscitation
Blood-culture results and suspected infection source
Whether vasopressors are required to maintain mean arterial pressure
priorityActions: Initiate rapid IV isotonic crystalloid fluid resuscitation per sepsis protocol.
Activate urgent sepsis escalation and prepare to initiate vasopressor support if hypotension persists after fluids.
reasoning: Persistent fever in severe neutropenia indicates a high-risk infection, while hypotension, delayed capillary refill, oliguria, tachycardia, and elevated lactate demonstrate systemic hypoperfusion. The available data support neutropenic sepsis with hypoperfusion; septic shock cannot be confirmed without knowing the response to adequate fluid resuscitation and whether vasopressors are required.
stemEvidence: Confirmed severe neutropenia with persistent fever
Urine output of only 60 mL over 4 hours
Elevated lactate of 3.2 mmol/L despite initial empiric antibiotics
